incident.title: ProductApiLatencyHigh
incident.description: product-api p99 latency 4.2s (SLO 400ms) and 5xx rate 9% for 11 minutes. Product pages are slow or failing for most customers.

initial_context: Recent deploys, shown before any check: 13:48-13:55 UTC product-api v5.3.0 rolled to 6 of 12 instances (the other 6 still run v5.2.9). Change summary: 'Shorten product-detail cache TTL from 10 minutes to 2 minutes so price changes show sooner; add an inventory lookup to the product page.' No other deploys today.

hypotheses.deploy: The product-api v5.3.0 deploy introduced a regression that causes the errors and latency.
hypotheses.cache: A problem with the product cache is behind the errors and latency.
hypotheses.db_slow: The database itself is degraded and slow to answer.
hypotheses.traffic: A traffic increase exceeds what the service can handle.
hypotheses.dependency: A downstream service the product API calls is slow or failing.
hypotheses.network: Network problems between the API and its backends are causing timeouts.

errors_by_version.description: product-api 5xx rate and p99 latency split by application version.
errors_by_version.result: 14:00-14:15 UTC. v5.2.9 (6 instances): 5xx 7.1%, p99 3.6s. v5.3.0 (6 instances): 5xx 11.4%, p99 4.9s. Both versions were under 0.3% 5xx and 180ms p99 before 14:04. First errors on both versions at 14:04:10.

deploy_diff.description: The code diff between product-api v5.2.9 and v5.3.0.
deploy_diff.result: 2 files changed. cache.py: PRODUCT_DETAIL_TTL = 600 -> 120 (seconds). product_page.py: adds one call to inventory-service GET /stock/{sku} per product page, cached for 30s. No changes to database access, connection pools or timeouts.

cache_events.description: Events for product-cache, the Redis cluster product-api reads through.
cache_events.result: 14:03:12 UTC product-cache primary node replaced during scheduled host maintenance (infra ticket INFRA-4471). The replacement started with an empty dataset: persistence is disabled on this cluster. Replication to the new primary completed 14:03:40 with 0 keys. No errors reported by the cluster since.

db_metrics.description: products-db CPU, query rate and query time over the last hour.
db_metrics.result: CPU 22% until 14:03, 91% from 14:04. Queries per second 1,100 until 14:03, 13,800 at 14:05, 9,200 at 14:15. Mean query time 3ms normally, 240ms since 14:04, with the same statements as before (product lookups by id). No slow-query or lock alerts. Replication healthy.

request_rate.result: Requests per second: 13:45 3,050; 14:00 3,120; 14:05 3,090; 14:15 3,040. Same-hour average over the last 4 weeks: 3,200.

inventory_latency.result: p50 12ms, p99 38ms, errors 0.02% over the last hour; unchanged since before 14:00. Called only by v5.3.0 instances.

network_stats.description: Packet loss, retransmits and connection errors between product-api and its backends.
network_stats.result: Packet loss 0.00%, TCP retransmits 0.1% (normal 0.1%), no connection resets or DNS errors in the last hour.

product_logs.result: From 14:04:05, about 2,900 lines per second on both versions: 'cache miss for product:{id}, loading from products-db'. From 14:04:40, about 180 per second: 'timeout acquiring products-db connection after 2000ms'. No new exception types on v5.3.0.

guidance: A failed query (like a timeout or a locked table) means the check itself could not complete. It is not evidence that nothing happened. An empty result from a wrong service name means the query was malformed, not that there is nothing to find. Neither should be cited as evidence in a root cause analysis.
